findings.evidence: "Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the stipend budget each quarter."
findings.fix: Either explain how budget-tracking and log-publishing relate (e.g., "The IT asset group tracks the budget that People Ops reports on"), or drop "Similarly" and state each team's role independently.
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies the IT asset group's budget-tracking is parallel to the People Ops office's log-publishing, but these are different activities performed by different teams; the connector creates a false equivalence and leaves the actual division of responsibility unclear.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter" vs. "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Merge the two "Overview" sections into one and state a single, correct owner and publication cadence for the reimbursement log.
findings.location: Program Overview (paragraph 1) vs. Overview (nine sections later)
findings.violation: The document states twice, under two different headings, who publishes the reimbursement log and how often, and the two statements contradict each other on both the owner (People Ops vs. benefits team) and the cadence (quarterly vs. per open-enrollment period).

findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time." appears verbatim in both sections.
findings.fix: Delete the duplicate sentence and keep it in only one place.
findings.violation: The same sentence is duplicated word-for-word in two separate sections, indicating the document was not deduplicated after merging content.

findings.evidence: "If the position counts as full-time, the stipend can apply... Only once every condition above is met does the home-office equipment stipend become available"
findings.fix: Rewrite as a single sentence, e.g., "The stipend is available only if the position is full-time, the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, and the request arrives before the benefit year ends."
findings.violation: Each conditional sentence is phrased as independently sufficient ("the stipend can apply"), but the closing sentence says all three conditions are jointly required (AND), so the paragraph reads as internally contradictory about whether the conditions are alternatives or cumulative requirements.

findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Remove this sentence from the policy, or replace it with a general rule about backup-reviewer coverage and sign-off responsibilities.
findings.violation: This is a narrative account of a one-off staffing incident, not a general policy rule, and it doesn't belong in a document meant to describe the standard process for all employees; it also implies indefinite delay, which conflicts with the fixed timeline given later.

findings.evidence: "The request is reviewed within two business days."
findings.fix: Reconcile the two sections - either state that the two-day timeline assumes normal reviewer availability and describe an escalation path for absences, or remove the anecdote in "How to Apply."
findings.violation: This firm two-business-day commitment directly contradicts the preceding "How to Apply" section, which describes the review being delayed because the backup reviewer wasn't informed of the sign-off requirement.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Clarify whether the approved list is binding or advisory, and rewrite the sentence in plain language consistent with the rest of the document.
findings.violation: This contradicts the Approval Timeline section's statement that "the manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list," leaving it unclear whether approval is bound by the checklist/approved list or overridden by manager discretion. The legalistic phrasing ("pursuant to," "notwithstanding") also breaks from the plain-language tone used elsewhere.

findings.evidence: Eligibility: "reimbursement is not available without a completed receipt. A scanned copy sent by email satisfies the requirement." / Required Documentation: "employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Consolidate all receipt-related requirements (submission format and retention period) into the "Required Documentation" section.
findings.location: Required Documentation section vs. Eligibility section
findings.violation: Receipt requirements are split across two non-adjacent sections, making the documentation rules hard to find as a single reference.

findings.evidence: "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time."
findings.fix: Replace with a direct statement, e.g., "The deposit reimburses the employee for costs already paid," or delete the sentence as redundant with the prior one.
findings.violation: The phrase "at this point in time" is vague filler with no clear referent, and the sentence as a whole restates "reimbursement" in a confusing, roundabout way.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g., "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence switches to second-person ("You"/"we"), breaking from the third-person voice ("the employee," "the manager") used throughout the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Remove "Similarly" or replace it with a neutral transition like "Additionally."
findings.violation: "Similarly" is used to connect this sentence to the prior one about equipment condition and photo checks, but a per-device-category limit is not similar to a condition/inspection requirement, making the transition illogical.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Either define "stipend item" explicitly and explain how it differs from "stipend," or rename the section and revert to third-person voice.
findings.violation: A section titled "Terminology Notes" should define terms, but it never defines "stipend item" or distinguishes it from "stipend" used elsewhere; it also shifts to second-person voice again, inconsistent with the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Remove this duplicate content or merge it into the "How to Apply" section.
findings.violation: This restates portal submission and tracking already described in "How to Apply," creating redundant, scattered process documentation.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Consolidate all request-process steps into the "How to Apply" section and remove this section.
findings.violation: This one-sentence section fragments the request process into a third location (alongside "How to Apply" and "Terminology Notes") without adding new information, making the overall procedure hard to follow as a single sequence.

findings.evidence: "## Overview" duplicating the earlier "## Program Overview" heading
findings.fix: Merge this section's content into "Program Overview" and delete the duplicate heading.
findings.violation: Using a near-duplicate heading name for a different (and contradictory) set of content confuses document navigation and suggests unmerged draft content.

findings.evidence: "Once approved, the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle."
findings.fix: Specify a single owner for scheduling/issuing the reimbursement payment and remove the conflicting claim from the other section.
findings.violation: This conflicts with the Reimbursement Amounts section's statement that "the finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle," leaving it ambiguous whether the benefits team or the finance office is responsible for issuing payment.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Add this review step to the "Approval Timeline" section and clarify its effect on the stated turnaround time.
findings.violation: This introduces an additional review step and dollar threshold that is never mentioned in the "Approval Timeline" section, so it's unclear how this review fits into (or extends) the stated two-business-day timeline.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Move this rule into "Restrictions and Exceptions" alongside the one-device-per-category rule.
findings.violation: This is a new restriction on requests that logically belongs with, but is disconnected from, the "Restrictions and Exceptions" section.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the vendor list each quarter. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Either rename the section to match its content (e.g., "Vendor List") and explain the vendor list's purpose, or replace the content with actual guidance on where employees direct questions.
findings.violation: The section heading promises answers to questions or update information, but the content is about an unrelated, previously unmentioned "vendor list," with no contact information, FAQ, or explanation of how the vendor list relates to the equipment stipend.
